fields.Text:
Hypersensitivity types:
- I: {{c1::IgE}}
- II: antibodies against {{c2::cell-surface}} or matrix antigens
- III: {{c3::immune complexes}}
- IV: {{c4::T cells}}
fields.Extra:
- Hypersensitivity = tissue damage mediated by the immune system
- Types I, II and III are antibody-mediated; type IV is cell-mediated

fields.Text: Type II HSRs can cause pathology by inducing {{c1::inflammation}} by antibodies depositing on cell surfaces, which in turn activates complement
fields.Extra:
- e.g., Goodpasture syndrome, rheumatic fever, hyperacute transplant rejection, bullous pemphigoid

- Leads to generation of C3a/C5a to attract neutrophils and other proinflammatory cells; or initiates Fc receptor-mediated inflammation

- In bullous pemphigoid: binding of autoantibodies → recruitment of neutrophils → stimulation of complement mediated inflammation and destruction of BP180





- Complement and Fc receptors bring neutrophils and macrophages, which release enzymes and oxygen radicals

fields.Text:
What is the result when thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulins (in Graves disease) bind to TSH receptors of the thyroid gland?

{{c1::They stimulate secretion of T3 and T4}}
fields.Extra:
- Thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulins (TSI) are autoantibodies that bind to and activate TSH receptors on thyroid epithelial cells

- This leads to increased secretion of thyroid hormones (T3 and T4) and thyroid gland growth, causing hyperthyroidism and a diffuse goiter

- This mechanism is characteristic of Graves disease, the most common cause of hyperthyroidism



- Instead of blocking the receptor, the antibody mimics TSH, so the thyroid is stimulated

fields.Text:
Which blood transfusion reaction is caused by host antibodies against donor ABO blood groups or foreign antigen on donor RBCs?

{{c1::Acute hemolytic transfusion reaction (AHTR)}}
fields.Extra:
- IgM isohemagglutinins formed naturally in response to bacterial flora cause opsonization and complement activation on donor RBCs, leading to hemolysis

- ABO incompatibility is mediated by the complement / IgM, whereas the foreign antigens are opsonized and cleared by the spleen



- Natural anti-A and anti-B antibodies are IgM: type A people have anti-B, type B have anti-A, type O have both and type AB none

fields.Extra:
- Poison ivy produces urushiol, which covalently binds to proteins on keratinocytes

- Sensitization phase: Langerhans cells uptake haptens (random skin proteins covalently bind urushiol), travel to draining lymph nodes, and interact with CD4+ / CD8 T cells (takes 10-14 days)

- Following sensitization / re-exposure to urushiol, the hapten is taken up by skin cells (e.g., keratinocytes), which are targeted by CD8 CTLs



- Contact dermatitis is delayed and T-cell mediated, so it is not type I even though it is called allergy

fields.Text:
Delayed hypersensitivity:
- sensitization: dendritic cells prime {{c1::naive T}} cells
- re-exposure: {{c2::Th1}} cells release IFN-γ
- IFN-γ activates {{c3::macrophages}}, which damage tissue
fields.Extra:
- The reaction takes about 48 h to peak because T cells and macrophages must be recruited
- CD8 T cells can instead kill the target directly

fora_do_recorte: Fotografias clínicas (pele, glomérulo, pulmão, esclerose múltipla, artrite), figuras de livro e imunofluorescência (lâminas 4–8, 16, 19–26, 32–38, 63–81): ilustram, não ensinam alvo.
Diagnóstico (Coombs, prick test, IgE específica, patch test), tratamento (adrenalina, Rhogan, corticoide) e fármacos: clínica e farmacologia.

Doenças por tipo (pênfigo, Goodpasture, púrpura, poliarterite, lúpus, artrite reumatoide, esclerose múltipla, diabetes, filariose): a aula é de mecanismo geral, não de doenças (F-20261021-CLAUDE-04); só entram exemplos que ilustram um mecanismo.
Dados epidemiológicos e hereditariedade da atopia, níveis de IgE em atópicos (lâminas 36–40, 45–47): ilustração sem cobrança.
